verdict: Motorola Solutions grew sales 12% to $3.4B on public-safety demand, but a $114M 'other charges' line and acquisition costs trimmed GAAP profit 9% to $512M — its non-GAAP EPS was $4.69.

kpis.label: Non-GAAP EPS
kpis.note: excludes other charges, acquisition amortization and stock pay

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Radios, video cameras and the networks behind them — land mobile radio systems for police, fire and other public-safety users, plus fixed video security.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Long-term service and software contracts: maintaining radio networks, command-center software and monitoring — recurring revenue that smooths the hardware cycle.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling to governments and enterprises, plus the back office.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Next-generation radios, cameras and AI-assisted command-center software.

opex.name: Other charges
opex.note: A net charge this quarter. In recent periods this line has included gains from the Hytera trade-secret litigation (Hytera paid $73M in the first nine months of 2026), alongside legal and other items.

opex.name: Intangibles amortization
opex.note: Write-down of technology bought in acquisitions — Motorola buys video and software companies regularly.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $107M, partly offset by $8M of other income.

takeaways.title: Public safety keeps spending
takeaways.text: Sales rose 12% in both North America and international markets, with acquisition contributions of $211M; management raised full-year guidance to about $13.05B of revenue.

takeaways.title: The GAAP dip is in the adjustments
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $4.69 vs $3.06 GAAP. The $114M of other charges and $97M of acquisition amortization explain most of the gap between the two profit stories.

takeaways.title: Services are the ballast
takeaways.text: Services brought in 41% of sales and grew 9% — multi-year contracts with governments that keep paying regardless of hardware cycles.

footerNote: This is Motorola Solutions' fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended October 3, 2026). The chart's sources are its reported sales split — products vs services; its reportable segments (Products & Systems Integration, Software & Services) grew 12% and 13% respectively.
